scenario: A 60-year-old male presents with abdominal pain, fever, hypotension, tachycardia, and findings consistent with intra-abdominal sepsis/cholangitis. The scenario focuses on early sepsis workup, intravenous fluid resuscitation, vasopressor support, deterioration to PEA arrest, and post-resuscitation management.

messages.content: You've got a high fever and your blood pressure's on the low side, so I need some quick answers. What's been bothering you, and when did it start?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need to be straight with you. You have a gallstone blocking your bile duct, and that blockage has become infected and spread into your bloodstream. It's life-threatening — your blood has turned dangerously acidic and your kidneys are failing. I'm giving you a medication, sodium bicarbonate, to fight the acid in your blood right now, but that only buys time. What will actually fix this is an urgent procedure to drain that blocked duct, and we're arranging it now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Sodium bicarbonate is up and going in now.
